chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Abu al-Hasan-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about one who forgot to perform al-Mulzamah (standing between the corner and the wall) in the last circuit of his Tawaf until he passed the Yemeni Corner: Is it permissible for him to perform it between the Yemeni Corner and the Stone, or should he leave it? He said, 'He should leave the Mulzamah and proceed.' And regarding one who combined ten circuits or more or fewer: Is he allowed to perform one Mulzamah in the last one? He said, 'I do not like that.'

The boundary of the Tawaf by the House, such that whoever exits it has not been a circumambulator of the House and has no Tawaf, is that he circumambulates between the Maqam (Station of Abraham) and the House. So whoever passes it or moves away from it, his Tawaf is not valid.

key_terms.أَسَابِيعَ: Asabi': Plural of Sabi', meaning circuits of Tawaf
key_terms.الرُّكْنِ الْيَمَانِيِّ: The Yemeni Corner: The corner of the Kaaba facing Yemen
key_terms.الطَّوَافِ: Tawaf: The ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْمَقَامِ: Al-Maqam: The Station of Abraham, located near the Kaaba
key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَمَ: Al-Mulzamah: The spot between the Yemeni Corner of the Kaaba and its wall where pilgrims stand to supplicate

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to perform Mulzamah during Tawaf?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic status of *al-Mulzamah* as a recommended (mustahabb) act rather than a pillar, evidenced by the Imam’s ruling that forgetting it requires no compensation. It further establishes the spatial validity of *Tawaf* by defining its boundary as the area between the Maqam Ibrahim and the Kaaba, ensuring the circumambulation remains within the sacred precincts.
